title: Beatrix and the Smile
premise: Folklorist Vesper Crane returns to the village of Hollowmere to record its dying songs, but the villagers refuse to sing any tune twice, and her ancestral house begins reflecting rooms one second late—then one second early. She learns the Crane founders bound something beneath the village with a ritual sung in unison, a ritual that requires every living descendant's voice, and that her seven years of self-imposed invisibility were the thing keeping it asleep. As the reflection-world begins arriving before events happen, Vesper must recover the scattered verses from the villagers' guarded memories and finish the ritual before the smile in the mirrors—her own face, worn by something else—steps out ahead of her. She completes it by singing alone, accepting that she will be remembered only as the song's final verse, and the mirrors fall silent at the cost of her reflection, her name, and the village's memory of her.
about_author: Ivo Galloway is the pen name of a former archivist of regional song collections who spent a decade cataloguing folk melodies no community would perform twice. They write horror from a farmhouse whose windows they have never once covered.

chapters.title: The Village That Sings Once
chapters.summary: Vesper arrives in Hollowmere with recording equipment and a letter of introduction no one will honor. POV: Vesper. She coaxes one old woman, Maren, into a single verse of a harvest song before Maren goes pale and stops. Emotional beat: wary curiosity curdling into unease.

chapters.title: House of Late Rooms
chapters.summary: In her inherited family house, Vesper notices her bathroom mirror lags a half-second behind her movements. POV: Vesper. She blames exhaustion, old plumbing, her own need to be startled. Emotional beat: rationalization as armor.

chapters.title: What Maren Wouldn't Repeat
chapters.summary: Vesper plays Maren her own recording; the woman flees the room. POV: Vesper, with a brief Maren interlude. Maren burns a scrap of paper bearing a musical notation. Emotional beat: the first confirmation the refusal is fear, not superstition.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Small Noises
chapters.summary: Flashback to the noises Vesper spent seven years explaining: footsteps above, humming in walls, her name tried in different voices. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: the dawning cost of a life spent not looking.

chapters.title: The Second Delay
chapters.summary: Every mirror in the house now reflects one full second late. POV: Vesper. She tests it obsessively with a stopwatch, then watches her reflection smile before she does. Emotional beat: terror breaking through denial.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: In the attic, Vesper finds the Crane family ledger: a list of names, dates, and a ritual described in fragments—'sung whole or not at all.' POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: inheritance reimagined as obligation.

chapters.title: Interview with the Innkeeper
chapters.summary: The innkeeper Tam admits the village once sang together, every solstice, until 1974, when 'the Cranes stopped needing us.' POV: Tam, framed by Vesper's notes. Emotional beat: communal guilt surfacing.

chapters.title: The Face That Waits
chapters.summary: Vesper's reflection begins moving independently during the delay, arranging its face into a patient smile. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: violation—the self as contested territory.

chapters.title: Maren's Confession
chapters.summary: Dying Maren tells Vesper the 1974 ritual failed because one Crane refused to sing: Vesper's mother. The thing beneath was only lulled, not bound. POV: Maren, then Vesper. Emotional beat: grief for a mother revealed as deserter.

chapters.title: Verse One: The Naming
chapters.summary: Vesper deciphers the first verse from the ledger and hums it; the mirrors snap into perfect sync—too perfect. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: the intoxication and danger of progress.

chapters.title: The Children's Rhyme
chapters.summary: Village children skip-rope to a corrupted version of verse two. Their teacher forbids it; that night the schoolhouse windows all reflect a room no one is in. POV: the teacher, Edith. Emotional beat: innocence as unwitting courier.

chapters.title: Tam's Bargain
chapters.summary: Tam offers the second verse in exchange for Vesper leaving before the solstice. POV: Tam. He believes distance can save her; the reader sees it cannot. Emotional beat: protection shaped as exile.

chapters.title: Reflections Ahead of Time
chapters.summary: The mirrors begin showing events before they occur: a broken cup, a red door, a figure on the stairs. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: helplessness—prophecy without agency.

chapters.title: The Undercroft
chapters.summary: Vesper finds a sealed room beneath the house: a circle of thirteen chairs, each facing a wall-sized mirror, all dark. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: dread of a stage prepared long ago.

chapters.title: Verse Two: The Turning
chapters.summary: Vesper reconstructs verse two from the children's rhyme. Singing it, she sees the dark mirrors flicker with a room that is almost hers. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: momentum shadowed by certainty of a trap.

chapters.title: Edith's Archive
chapters.summary: Teacher Edith reveals a hidden cache of confiscated student papers—decades of children transcribing verses they heard in dreams. POV: Edith. Emotional beat: quiet heroism, and horror at what dreams the village has been having.

chapters.title: The Smiling Man in the Square
chapters.summary: A stranger arrives whom no mirror will reflect, smiling at everyone. Villagers begin forgetting small things—their dogs' names, their own middle names. POV: rotating villagers. Emotional beat: erosion of identity as contagion.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Omits
chapters.summary: Vesper discovers a thirteenth name scraped from the ledger: not a founder—a vessel. The ritual doesn't banish the thing; it gives it a face to wear. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: betrayal across generations.

chapters.title: Verse Three: The Borrowing
chapters.summary: From Edith's archive Vesper assembles verse three, which can only be sung by two voices. She and Edith sing it; every mirror in Hollowmere shatters except Vesper's bedroom glass, which now shows the undercroft, occupied. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: alliance forged, trap sprung.

chapters.title: The Solstice Deadline
chapters.summary: Tam's almanac confirms the ritual must complete at solstice—nine days. The smiling man is seen standing in the square all night, not moving. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: the clock becoming audible.

chapters.title: Mother's Letters
chapters.summary: Vesper finds letters her mother hid: she refused to sing because the vessel chosen in 1974 was Vesper, then an infant. Her refusal saved her daughter and doomed the village's memory. POV: Vesper reading. Emotional beat: love reframed as the original sin.

chapters.title: Verse Four: The Hollowing
chapters.summary: Verse four requires the singer to name what they'd give up. Vesper practices it alone; each attempt takes a memory—her university, a lover, the smell of her mother's kitchen. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: sacrifice made literal and priced.

chapters.title: The Village Forgets Edith
chapters.summary: Edith's students stop recognizing her; the archive papers blank themselves. Edith, fading, urges Vesper to run. POV: Edith. Emotional beat: the cost of proximity to the ritual.

chapters.title: The Smiling Man Speaks
chapters.summary: The man finally addresses Vesper: he is the thing the founders caught, and the 'ritual' was always an invitation—he has been waiting for a Crane willing to finish it. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: the revelation inverting the quest.

chapters.title: Verse Five: The False Verse
chapters.summary: Vesper finds a fifth verse in the ledger and sings it; her reflection steps out of the mirror and walks into the village wearing her face. She realizes verse five was the trap—the founders' handwriting changes halfway through. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: the lowest point; she has unmade herself.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Isn't Vesper
chapters.summary: The double charms the village, completing preparations for solstice. Villagers who resisted begin smiling too. POV: Tam, watching the double with terrible ease. Emotional beat: usurpation and the horror of being replaced without protest.

chapters.title: Locked Out of Her Own Life
chapters.summary: The house no longer recognizes Vesper; doors open for the double. She sleeps in the undercroft among the thirteen chairs. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: exile inside one's own inheritance.

chapters.title: Maren's Last Verse
chapters.summary: Dying Maren, lucid one final hour, teaches Vesper the true sixth verse her own grandmother smuggled out in 1974—a verse not in the ledger, sung to unmake the invitation rather than complete it. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: a torch passed at the last possible moment.

chapters.title: What the Ritual Actually Is
chapters.summary: Vesper assembles the truth: thirteen founders, thirteen verses, one sung in unison by the whole village—not to bind the thing, but to give it a bounded shape so it could be lived alongside. Her mother's refusal left it shapeless and hungry. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: understanding as both relief and condemnation.

chapters.title: Rallying the Unwilling
chapters.summary: Vesper, half-forgotten herself, goes door to door asking the village to sing. Most refuse. Edith, barely remembered, stands in the square and begins the first verse alone. POV: Edith. Emotional beat: courage as contagion, finally the good kind.

chapters.title: The Double's Counter-Song
chapters.summary: The double sings the false fifth verse from the church steps, splitting the village's voices. Some sing with her. The mirrors in the shattered shopfronts begin showing tomorrow. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: a war fought entirely in harmony and discord.

chapters.title: Verse Seven: The Debt
chapters.summary: Vesper learns verse seven demands a name freely surrendered. She writes her own name on the ledger's scraped line and feels it begin to leave her—memories of herself thinning like frost. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: chosen erasure.

chapters.title: Solstice Eve
chapters.summary: The village gathers or hides; the smiling man takes his seat in the thirteenth chair. Vesper, unrecognizable even to herself in the dark mirrors, takes the first chair. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: terrible calm before the singing.

chapters.title: The Singing
chapters.summary: The ritual begins. Verses one through four rise from the village in ragged unison; the double fights each one with the false verse. Edith's voice fails; Tam, who never sang in his life, carries the line. POV: rotating among the singers. Emotional beat: collective, trembling defiance.

chapters.title: Verse Six: The Unmaking
chapters.summary: At the climax Vesper sings Maren's smuggled sixth verse, and the false verse dies in the double's throat. The thing in the thirteenth chair loses its borrowed smile and shows its true shape: a hunger with no face, waiting to be given one. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: triumph immediately shadowed by the final cost.

chapters.title: The Name Given
chapters.summary: Vesper completes verse seven, surrendering her name into the bounded shape. The thing takes it—not her face, not her body, only the name and the memory of her—and settles into the mirrors as a presence that reflects rooms exactly on time. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: grief and completion in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Village That Forgot
chapters.summary: Morning. The village remembers a ritual and a solstice, and a folklorist who 'passed through.' Maren's grave gains an unexplained second marker. Edith alone keeps a single page that won't blank. POV: Edith. Emotional beat: the loneliness of being the only witness.

chapters.title: The Woman Without a Reflection
chapters.summary: Vesper, alive and unnamed, packs her recordings. In the last unbroken mirror she casts no image at all—she has become the one thing in Hollowmere the mirrors won't hold. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: freedom and erasure indistinguishable.

chapters.title: Songs Sung Twice
chapters.summary: Vesper plays her recordings for the villagers, who now sing the old songs twice, even three times, weeping without knowing why. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: mourning transformed into gift.

chapters.title: The Smile in the Glass
chapters.summary: Leaving Hollowmere, Vesper passes a service-station mirror that reflects her after all—one second late, smiling a smile she didn't make. She smiles back, and keeps walking. POV: Vesper, closing frame. Emotional beat: uneasy peace; the inheritance continues.
